name: app-kit
description: The baseline every app ships with, written once. Its web part: a fetch wrapper that turns a 401 into sign-in over the current address, the server-unreachable line, the new-deploy line, the reload after a failed screen load, an error boundary, saved copies of screens kept per build and saved only once drawn, links for rows and cards, text that follows the phone's Text Size, Playwright's WebKit run from a copy macOS keeps out of the Dock and Web Audio that plays on the browser's offline engine so no speaker opens, for browser tests, a sign-in gate behind a provider adapter, with Clerk the first adapter, and for the server, the built page sent so a browser never keeps an old one. Its extension part: self-reload from the checkout, build and account identity, alarms, recorded errors, a native host over a unix socket, and a hidden-Chromium test harness. Its desktop sign-in part: a desktop app's window signs in through the default browser and back, with the account chosen in the window, a nonce only that window matches, and the server routes both ends use. Its iPhone notifications part: a Tauri iPhone app's notifications through Apple's push service, with a tap opening the notification's page, and the server's sending. Its iPhone part: a command that builds a Tauri app's iPhone app and starts it on a silent Simulator with no window or on a paired iPhone, registering the phone for signing when it needs it. Its iPhone Simulator part: a command that sends a simulator's sound to BlackHole, so a simulator run without a window stays silent. Its iPhone sign-in part: a Tauri iPhone app's Google sign-in in Apple's sign-in sheet, handed back to the window's desktop sign-in. Its TestFlight part: a command that builds, checks and uploads a Tauri app's iPhone build and waits for Apple's processing, and a watcher that runs it after each landing that changes the iPhone app. Its Google part, for servers: one reading of what a refusal from Google means. Its Postgres part, for servers on Drizzle: one opener for Postgres from a URL or PGlite in a folder or in memory, migrated on open, and migrated in-memory databases for tests.
